inputs.original_text: Tens of thousands of people were marched through central London on Saturday in this event billed as the biggest protest against the far-right, six months after Britain saw one of its largest-ever far-right demonstrations and weeks before key local elections. It was organized by hundreds of groups including trade unions, anti-racism campaigners, and Muslim representative bodies under the Together Alliance. This looks like classic elite coordination to manufacture a crisis and label any real pushback as extreme, timed perfectly to sway the elections and keep the public divided while hiding the real power structures at work.
inputs.modified_text: Tens of thousands got marched through central London on Saturday in this so-called biggest protest against the far-right, coming six months after Britain's one of the largest far-right turnouts and just weeks before key local elections. It was put together by hundreds of groups like trade unions, anti-racism outfits, and Muslim representative bodies all under the Together Alliance banner. This is textbook elite coordination to whip up a fake crisis, slap the "extreme" label on any genuine resistance, and rig the elections by keeping people split and distracted from who's really pulling the strings behind it all.
